sections.title: Purpose of Creation & Ma'rifah
sections.summary: Human beings were created to worship and know God (Q 51:56); ma'rifah deepens that worship into ihsan.
bullets: Worship encompasses knowledge, remembrance, and ethical action.
Knowing God transforms ritual into conscious devotion.
Classical scholars link ma'rifah with the heart's awakening.

sections.title: Sources of Knowledge about Allah
sections.summary: Revelation, prophetic example, and the created world provide complementary windows into the Divine Names.
bullets: Qur'an names God explicitly and implicitly through signs.
Prophetic character manifests mercy, justice, and balance.
Creation mirrors divine attributes in ordered complexity.
Sound reason operates within the guidance of revelation.

sections.title: Classical Arguments for God's Existence
sections.summary: Theological traditions employ rational proofs that point to a Necessary Being with perfect attributes.
bullets: Kalam cosmological argument: the universe began; therefore it has a transcendent cause.
Argument from contingency: contingent beings require a necessary existent.
Teleological reasoning notes fine-tuning and purposeful order.
Moral argument: objective values imply a perfectly just source.

sections.title: Science, Cosmology, and Awe
sections.summary: Modern discoveries in physics and biology expand horizons for contemplating the Divine Names.
bullets: Cosmic fine-tuning suggests delicate calibration supportive of life.
Astrobiology invites humility about humanity's place and role.
Quantum and complexity sciences highlight limits of reductionism.
Awe and wonder can nurture gratitude and stewardship.

sections.title: Psychology of Faith and Remembrance
sections.summary: Psychological studies show that consistent remembrance fosters resilience, meaning, and moral behavior.
bullets: Dhikr regulates stress and cultivates emotional balance.
Secure attachment to God correlates with compassion.
Narratives and journaling support integration of belief and action.
Mindfulness practices align with prophetic presence (hudur).

sections.title: Sociology & History of Ma'rifah
sections.summary: Communities transmit ma'rifah through scholarship, spiritual guilds, and lived ethical models.
bullets: Early Muslim societies paired jurisprudence with spiritual counsel.
Sufi orders emphasized character refinement and service.
Women scholars safeguarded hadith chains and devotional poetry.
Modern revivalists call for holistic taqwa amid rapid change.

sections.title: Practical Devotional Program
sections.summary: Structured routines help seekers internalize the Names through reflection, worship, and service.
bullets: Daily: recite selected Names with contemplation and journal insights.
Weekly: study a research section and share learnings in community.
Monthly: dedicate charity or service in light of a chosen Name.
Seasonal: retreat or digital detox to renew focus on God.

sections.title: Ethics, Boundaries, and Adab
sections.summary: Respectful theology avoids anthropomorphism, spiritual pride, and sectarian harm.
bullets: Affirm divine transcendence while embracing relational Names.
Guard the heart from riya (showing off) and seek sincerity.
Follow madhhab guidance in worship and creed matters.
Consult scholars when facing complex doctrinal questions.
